podcasts.name: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Dismissal of Richard Berry
podcast.body: The Flares eventually dismissed Richard Berry from the group due to his extensive commitments to other recording projects and numerous other bands. "The Flares eventually got sick of Barry working on so many other people's records and singing with so many groups, and so he was out of the group"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Extensive Recording Under Multiple Names
podcast.body: Over several years, The Flares recorded and released tracks under various names, including The Hunters, and as solo records for Young Jesse, in addition to their work as The Flares. "Over the next couple of years, The Flares would record and release tracks under all sorts of names, as well as many Flair's records, they also release tracks as by The Hunters. As young Jesse Solo records"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Later Member Departures
podcast.body: After Richard Berry's departure, The Flares continued for years, but members gradually left for other groups. Thomas Fox joined The Cadets, who had a hit with "Stranded in the Jungle," and Cornell Gunter famously joined the classic lineup of The Coasters. "The Flares continued for years, though one at a time they left through other groups, Thomas Fox joined the cadets, who had a hit with Stranded in the Jungle, and most famously Cornel Gunter went on to join the classic lineup of the coasters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Name Change for Promotion
podcast.body: The group eagerly changed its name to The Flares upon signing with Flair Records, a Modern Records subsidiary, believing that sharing the label's name would enhance their chances of promotion. "The label suggested they changed their name to The Flares, and they eagerly agreed. Thinking the tip of their band had the same name as The Label, the label would be more likely to promote them."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Produced by Ike Turner
podcast.body: At one point, The Flares were produced by Ike Turner, who by then had transitioned from working with Sam Phillips to producing for the Beharry Brothers, owners of Modern Records. "The band was produced by Ag Turner, who by this point had moved on from working with Sam Phillips and was now working for the Beharry Brothers, who owned modern records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
